title: Communication Part A
description: A first-year writing and speaking course on reading, research, and composing clear arguments for academic audiences.
notes: UW general education: Communication A (or a placement score).

title: Communication Part B
description: An intermediate course with substantial writing or speaking practice, often in the student's field, building on a first-year communication course.

title: Ethnic Studies
description: A course on the history, culture, and experiences of racial and ethnic groups in the United States, chosen from an approved list.
notes: UW general education: one 3+ credit Ethnic Studies course.

title: World Language (first semester)
description: A first-semester course in a language other than English: basic speaking, listening, reading, and writing.
notes: L&S BS language requirement (third unit); the plan places four semesters.

title: World Language (second semester)
description: A second-semester course in a language other than English, continuing basic speaking, listening, reading, and writing.
notes: L&S BS language requirement (third unit); the plan places four semesters.

title: World Language (third semester)
description: A third-semester (intermediate) course in a language other than English, with more reading and conversation.
notes: L&S BS language requirement (third unit); the plan places four semesters.

title: World Language (fourth semester)
description: A fourth-semester (intermediate) course in a language other than English, with more reading, writing, and conversation.
notes: L&S BS language requirement (third unit); the plan places four semesters.

title: Linear Algebra
description: A linear algebra course: systems of linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors. Some versions are combined with differential equations, optimization, or multivariable calculus.
notes: Choice slot: Wisconsin's MATH 320, 340, 345, 341, or 375. Official descriptions are in data/raw/wisc/ (courses-math page).

title: Probability or Statistics
description: A probability or statistics course: probability models, random variables and distributions, and statistical estimation, testing, or regression.
notes: Choice slot: one of nine Wisconsin probability and statistics courses. Official descriptions are in data/raw/wisc/ (courses-stat and courses-math pages).

title: COMP SCI Theory
description: An upper-level theory course: either the design and analysis of algorithms (greedy, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, NP-completeness) or the theory of computation (automata, computability, complexity).
notes: Choice slot: Wisconsin's COMP SCI 577 (recommended) or COMP SCI 520. Official descriptions are in data/raw/wisc/ (courses-comp_sci page).

title: COMP SCI Software/Hardware
description: An upper-level systems or software course chosen from a list, such as operating systems, software engineering, compilers, databases, computer architecture, networks, or security.
notes: Wisconsin: two courses (6-8 credits) from a list of 12.

title: COMP SCI Applications
description: An upper-level course on an application area of computing chosen from a list, such as numerical methods, optimization, artificial intelligence, graphics, computer vision, or human-computer interaction.
notes: Wisconsin: one course from a list of 13.

title: COMP SCI Elective
description: An upper-level computer science course chosen by the student from an approved list, including cross-listed courses in mathematics, statistics, and engineering.
notes: Wisconsin: two courses (6-8 credits) from the Electives list.

title: Social Science Breadth
description: A course in the social sciences, such as economics, political science, psychology, or sociology, chosen from courses with the social science designation.
notes: L&S BS breadth: 12 credits of social science.

title: Humanities Breadth
description: A course in the humanities, such as history, philosophy, art, or music, chosen from courses with the humanities designation.
notes: L&S BS breadth: 12 credits of humanities or literature, at least 6 of literature.

title: Literature Breadth
description: A course in literature, in English or another language, chosen from courses with the literature designation.
notes: L&S BS breadth: 12 credits of humanities or literature, at least 6 of literature.

title: Biological Science Breadth
description: A course in the biological sciences, such as biology, zoology, or botany, chosen from courses with the biological science designation.
notes: L&S BS breadth: natural science credits including biological science.

title: Physical Science Breadth
description: A course in the physical sciences, such as chemistry, physics, astronomy, or geoscience, chosen from courses with the physical science designation.
notes: L&S BS breadth: natural science credits including physical science.

title: Elective
description: Any course the student chooses, inside or outside the major, that counts toward the degree. Students often use free electives for a minor, extra courses in the major, or personal interests.
notes: Wisconsin: free electives to reach 120 credits.
